input: Create a personal brand style guide

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Whether this is for a solo creator, a professional in a corporate field, or an entrepreneur changes the tone, formality, and depth of the guide entirely.
A style guide can range from just a logo and colour palette to a full system covering typography, voice, photography style, and templates — knowing what to include prevents over- or under-building.
Where the brand will live (LinkedIn, Instagram, personal website, speaking engagements, etc.) dictates which formats and channels the guide needs to address.
Whether the user has an existing logo, colours, or prior brand assets determines whether this is a build-from-scratch project or a consolidation/refinement task.
The desired tone and personality of the brand (bold vs. understated, professional vs. casual) shapes every creative decision in the guide.
The intended format and tool for the guide (Notion, PDF, Canva, Google Doc) affects how it is structured and how easy it will be to share and maintain.
Knowing who will use the guide and for what purpose (just the user, a designer, a social media manager) defines how detailed and instructional it needs to be.

gold.taskTitle: Create a personal brand style guide
gold.taskDescription: Build a cohesive personal brand style guide that defines visual, tonal, and messaging standards for consistent self-presentation.

questions.title: What industry or professional role is this brand for?
questions.description: Identify the user's field (e.g. tech entrepreneur, freelance designer, executive coach) to calibrate the right tone and positioning for the guide.

questions.title: Which elements should the style guide cover?
questions.description: Determine the scope — e.g. logo, colour palette, typography, brand voice, messaging pillars, social media templates, or all of the above.

questions.title: Which platforms or channels will this brand appear on?
questions.description: Identify where the brand will be used (LinkedIn, Instagram, personal website, podcast, speaking decks, etc.) to ensure the guide addresses the right contexts.

questions.title: Do you already have any brand assets such as a logo or colours?
questions.description: Establish whether this is a build-from-scratch effort or a consolidation of existing visual and messaging elements.

questions.title: How would you describe the personality or tone of your brand?
questions.description: Capture the desired brand character — e.g. bold and disruptive, warm and approachable, polished and authoritative — to guide all creative decisions.

questions.title: What format or tool should the final guide be built in?
questions.description: Determine the deliverable format — Notion page, PDF, Canva document, Google Doc, Figma file, etc. — to structure the guide appropriately.

questions.title: Who will use this guide once it is finished?
questions.description: Clarify the audience for the guide itself — just the user, a hired designer, a VA, or a social media manager — to calibrate the level of detail and instruction needed.
